subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB158, landed 2026-09-02). The rule is Table 3's symbol-adjacency matrix. WHICH CELLS THE GRAMMAR CAN STILL PRODUCE WAS MEASURED, one probe program per cell, parsed through the real compiler rather than reasoned about: ten of the thirteen invalid cells are already hard parse errors ((ident,ident), (binop,binop), (binop,')'), (unary,binop), (unary,')'), ('(',binop), ('(',')'), (')',ident), (')',unary), (')','(')), and two more - (ident,'(') and its sibling - cannot form as an arithmetic PAIR at all because COBOL reads a '(' after an identifier as a subscript or reference-modifier. Exactly ONE cell was producible: (unary, unary). It is now screened by ExpressionFormationPass over the shared frontend rule, covering all THREE evaluating arms (ExpressionBinder.BindExprCore, CompileTimeExpressionEvaluator.EvalArith, and its SoleNumericLiteral reclassification probe, which used to fold `- - 5` to the literal 5). The screen reads TOKEN POSITIONS, not the tree, because SS8.3.3.3.2 rule 2 makes an ADJACENT sign part of the numeric literal - `- -2` is the PERMISSIBLE (unary, literal) pair while `- - 2` is the invalid one, and in the default lexer mode both emit MINUS MINUS INTEGERLIT. A grammar tier would have rejected both, i.e. rejected legal source. The over-rejection guard is pinned positively (golden R10/R11/R12 and three unit cases).
